name: A10-0024/2026 – Reinier Van Lanschot – Provisional agreement – Am 86
title: REPORT on the proposal for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council amending Regulations (EU) No 765/2008, (EU) 2016/424, (EU) 2016/425, (EU) 2016/426, (EU) 2023/1230, (EU) 2023/1542 and (EU) 2024/1781 as regards digitalisation and common specifications
part_text: AMENDMENTS BY THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT\* to the Commission proposal REGULATION (EU) 2026/… OF THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND OF THE COUNCIL of … amending Regulations ▌ (EU) 2016/424, (EU) 2016/425, (EU) 2016/426, (EU) 2023/1230, (EU) 2023/1542 and (EU) 2024/1781 as regards digitalisation and common specifications (Text with EEA relevance) THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND THE COUNCIL OF THE EUROPEAN UNION, Having regard to the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union, and in particular Article 114 thereof, Having regard to the proposal from the European Commission, After transmission of the draft legislative act to the national parliaments, Having regard to the opinion of the European Economic and Social Committee, Acting in accordance with the ordinary legislative procedure, Whereas: (1) Reporting requirements play a key role in ensuring the proper monitoring and the correct enforcement of legislation. The overall costs of reporting are balanced by the benefits they bring, in particular in ensuring compliance with key policy measures. However, in order to ensure that the intended purpose of reporting requirements is fulfilled and in order to limit the administrative burden, it is important to streamline those requirements. (2) In its communication of 16 March 2023 entitled ‘Long-term competitiveness of the EU: looking beyond 2030’, the Commission has committed to rationalising and simplifying reporting requirements, with the aim of reducing the burdens created by such requirements by 25 %, without undermining the related policy objectives. (3) In its Better Regulation Guidelines of 3 November 2021, the Commission promotes the ‘digital by default’ principle to support digital transformations, by facilitating digital-ready policies which consider the fast-evolving world of digitalisation and technology, and which are digital, interoperable, future-proof and agile by default. (4) The increasing importance of digitalisation in simplifying regulatory frameworks necessitates the reduction, harmonisation and modernisation of reporting requirements and the obligations of economic operators. In line with the efforts to accelerate digitalisation, it is essential to fully digitalise business-to-authority reporting and the obligations of economic operators when those obligations do not affect the protection and safety of consumers or place an excessive burden on economic operators.
